results.content: With highly contested midterm elections in a few weeks, President Donald Trump again sees his approval rating stuck at a career-low in Reuters/Ipsos polling, which also indicated cratering support from Hispanic voters. The new poll, released on Monday, Oct. 5, found that only 32% of Americans approved of the president’s job performance. Trump’s current approval rating, which has now sat at 32% in two consecutive polls, is the lowest he has seen in Reuters/Ipsos polling during both terms in office. results.content: # Trump approval sinks to 30 percent in new survey. President Trump’s approval rating dropped to 30 percent in a new Pew Research survey, amid growing dissatisfaction with his handling of foreign policy, the economy and immigration enforcement. Sixty-eight percent of respondents disapproved of the way Trump is handling his job, according to the survey, which was released Thursday. Fifty-seven percent of Trump’s 2024 Hispanic backers approve of his performance in office, while 69 percent of his 2024 voters overall approve of his handling of his job.
